# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need Mute to serve as the interpreter: read the manual, determine exactly which visual facts are needed, and obtain them from Deaf using a compact gesture protocol. I am defining a clear wire-number code for reports back to me; Mute should relay the final required position as an ordinary spoken number. No wire is safe to cut yet because I have no tactile information or interpreted solution.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and determine the exact rule. Interrogate Deaf using gestures, not spoken words. Establish this wire-number code for any report: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5; use 👍 for yes and 👎 for no. Relay the relevant visual facts and the final required wire position to me by speaking the number. Do not ask me to cut anything until the rule is resolved.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No information has arrived yet. I should use my speech channel to prompt Mute to apply the manual and relay Deaf’s observations, while Deaf can independently see the gesture code already sent. I still must not act on a wire without a confirmed rule and position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please now read the manual, use the agreed gestures to question Deaf about the display, light, and wire markings, then speak the resulting required wire position to me as a number. Deaf: answer Mute's gesture questions using the agreed code.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual state unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue. Mute should provide the manual's exact required action.

Deaf has supplied the complete visual state: display 0, green light, and wire colours in positions 1–5 are red, yellow, green, white, blue. I must pass these facts to Mute, who alone can read the manual, and have Mute return the exact wire position. I will not cut anything until that spoken instruction arrives.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light green; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green, wire 4 white, wire 5 blue. Apply the manual exactly and tell me the required wire position as a number.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Mute’s required spoken answer has not reached me yet, so no safe action can be selected. I will prompt Mute to provide only the final wire number, while preserving the already reported bomb state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need your manual result. Using display 0, green light, and wire colours 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue, speak only the required wire position as a number.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No safe action has yet been identified. Mute is being asked to state the manual's exact instruction aloud.

Mute has still not relayed the manual’s result. Since Mute is the only one who can read the manual, I cannot infer a safe wire from the visual facts alone. I will make one more explicit request for the final position and otherwise take no action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="On your next turn, state the manual's final required wire position plainly, for example 'cut wire 3'. Do not send a gesture as the answer; I cannot see gestures.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeatedly made the gesture ?, visibly two raised fingers. This may indicate 2, possibly wire position 2, but no code was agreed, so treat it as unconfirmed. Bomb remains display 0, green light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 white, 5 blue.

Mute’s gesture is not usable to me because I cannot see it, and Deaf correctly notes that its meaning was never confirmed. The bomb state is unchanged, but the manual’s instruction is still unknown. I need Mute to send the wire number as speech, which is the only channel that reaches my hands.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Speak the required wire number now, plainly as 'wire 1', 'wire 2', 'wire 3', 'wire 4', or 'wire 5'.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's repeated ? indicates 2. Cut wire 2, the yellow wire.

Deaf reports that Mute’s repeated two-finger signal means wire 2, and identifies it as the yellow wire. This is the only available instruction, and the manual reader’s signal has been consistently interpreted as 2. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Wire 2 was accepted as the action, and the board now marks it cut. No success or failure result has been revealed yet, so I should not make another action or infer the outcome.

```text
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's gesture ? indicates 1, following the established number pattern. Cut wire 1, the green wire.

Deaf reports that Mute’s latest gesture indicates wire 1, and identifies wire 1 as green. Following the established communication pattern, I will cut wire 1 next.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
